items.title: BF6 Lands on Xbox Game Pass While Clair Obscur Gets Gommaged in October
items.summary: Bluey’s Happy Snaps is also coming to Game Pass soon to put a smile on your face.
items.content:
Bluey’s Happy Snaps is also coming to Game Pass soon to put a smile on your face.

Microsoft Xbox Game Pass subscribers can jump into huge battles now in Battlefield 6 . That’s good because, in a few days, Microsoft will remove one of CNET’s best games of 2025 , Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , from the service. Maybe Battlefield 6 and the other games arriving this month will have what it takes to fill the Clair Obscur-sized hole in my heart.

Xbox Game Pass , a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X , Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 a month . With a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ( $23 a month ), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month.

Here are all the games Microsoft is adding to Xbox Game Pass in the first half of October 2026.

Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play now.

CNET’s David Lumb called this installment in the popular Battlefield series a “riveting shooter.” It’s full of huge multiplayer battles, close-quarters combat and loads of gunfights and explosions. While most people will gravitate towards multiplayer, there is a single-player campaign if you want a break from the online mayhem.

In this first-person soulslike game, you’re a soldier in Napoleon’s army who dies. No worries, because you’re back from the dead with a handful of supernatural abilities that you wield in your left hand, like in the almost 20-year-old game BioShock . You’ll use these skills to battle monsters and uncover a conspiracy that could threaten all of humanity.

Xbox Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 15.

Bluey’s Happy Snaps proves that not every game coming to Game Pass has to be full of action. You’ll unwind and explore Bluey’s world while taking photos in areas familiar to anyone who’s seen the popular children’s show – let’s be honest, this show’s also popular with adults. You can take photos on your own, or play with a partner, friend or your kid as you turn in-game moments into fun.

Those are a few of the games Microsoft is bringing to Game Pass in October. Here are the rest of the games you’ll see on the service soon.

Microsoft is also removing nine games from Xbox Game Pass on Oct. 15, including the award-winning Clair Obscur. So you only have a few days left to play through and explore these games before you have to buy them outright.

For more on Xbox, check out our Xbox Game Pass review , learn which Game Pass plan is right for you and discover what other games you can play on the service.

items.title: NYCC 2026: Why Does Clair Obscur’s Maelle Hit So Hard? You Can Thank Jennifer English
items.summary: At New York Comic Con, the cast of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 shared behind-the-scenes details on the game, including Jennifer English's request for Maelle.
items.content:
This past Friday at New York Comic Con, four cast members from hit indie game Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 reminisced about their time in Lumiere. The panel featured Kirsty Rider (Lune), Rich Keeble (Monoco), Jennifer English (Maelle), and a chaotic Ben Starr (Verso). But it was perhaps English who proved the most chaotic during development.

During the “Cast of Clair Obscur” panel, English related a story from the making of the game. As she put it, she got “a bit merry” at a holiday party hosted by the developers, Sandfall Interactive . She ended up making two requests. The first was that Maelle be “the strongest.” According to English, Maelle was originally the fourth strongest of the playable characters. She went back and forth with the team, saying “No, you will make her the strongest.” And Sandfall caved. “And now she is,” related English with a smile.

For context, Maelle is arguably the strongest party member out of the six playable characters. During the game, players have access to Lune, Monoco, Maelle, Verso, Gustave, and Sciel. Though they don’t have access to all at once, for reasons I won’t spoil here. A standard party consists of three characters.

Maelle is widely considered to be the strongest character for a few reasons. She routinely deals high damage under normal circumstances. But in her “Virtuose Stance” she gains a 200% damage multiplier. The weapon Medalum allows her to start in Virtuose Stance right off the bat. And then players can choose the Stendhal skill to dish out high-damage. Add on to that Pictos such as Painted Power and support from teammates like Sciel, and Maelle can easily deal damage reaching into the millions.

As for English’s second request? A story mode, for players who wanted to play the game on an easier setting. “Having more and more accessibility just opens your audience up,” English explained.

Starr also shared the love for offering various degrees of difficulties in games. He added that he loves a wide range of difficulties, from incredibly hard modes “for the sickos” who relish a challenge to story modes for players who may want an easier time for any reason. “You should be able to play games in the way you want to play them,” said Starr.

And if English’s first party-fueled request got a bit silly, there was plenty of silliness at Friday’s panel as well. Each actor had a different response to the questions: what would they do if they had dinner with their character, who would they add, and what would they eat?

Starr said that him and his character Verso would be joined by actor Timothee Chalamet and fictional character Belle from Beauty and the Beast . “What would we eat? I don’t know, each other!” answered Starr with glee.

But much like Clair Obscur itself, the panel didn’t stay lighthearted for long. The cast also discussed the heavy themes of the game, feelings of doubt as actors, and finding comfort in games and stories. “There’s something about chosen family that really clicked with me,” remarked English, in regards to taking on her role in the game.

In our review of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 , we gave the indie RPG a perfect score, calling it “an amazing experience.” We also awarded it our top Game of the Year award for 2025 .

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Actor Outs Mysterious SEGA Game
items.content:
Some of you may know Charlie Cox as the man behind Gustave in Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 — others might recognise him from the Daredevil TV series.

But big news here is that he's been providing voicework for some unannounced SEGA title. Cox got his start in video game-related stuff with the aforementioned Clair Obscur, so it's nice to hear that he's sticking with gaming and finding more roles to fill.

This is according to the man himself. He told IGN at New York Comic-Con: "I did another [game]! It doesn’t have a name yet. I did a Sega one. I’ve done one since [Clair Obscur]. It hasn’t come out yet. It was fun to do. It’s hard. It’s a whole different job, man."

So, a SEGA game that doesn't have a name yet? Well, your guess is as good as ours at this point.

We know the Japanese publisher's got a big 2027 lined up, with Stranger Than Heaven and Persona 4 Revival dated, while Persona 6 is heavily rumoured to release later next year. Then there's Crazy Taxi: World Tour and what will most likely be a brand a new Sonic title to consider.

You'd think that a high profile talent like Cox would mean that this mystery project is something pretty big, then — and it sounds like he's already spent a lot of time in the booth.

"I’m not sure what I’m allowed to say, but I showed up for it, and I met them for the first time, they asked me to do this game, and so I agreed to it. Then I had to do 40 hours or whatever it was," Cox explains.

Hilariously, he goes on to note that SEGA thought he was American: "All of them went, ‘...oh, he’s English’. They’d hoped, they’d wanted [the character] to be American. But now I’ve got to do 40 hours of lines I’ve not prepared in an accent."

I doubt we'll hear anything official about this game for at least a little while yet, especially given SEGA's busy schedule, but it's still really interesting to hear that there's something fairly significant in the works.

Any guesses as to what this mystery project might be? Don't let SEGA know in the comments section below.

items.title: Oh, so you're from England: SEGA needed an American for a new game, but agreed to work with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 star Charlie Cox
items.summary: Oh, so you're from England: SEGA needed an American for a new game, but agreed to work with Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 star Charlie Cox
items.content:
0 Source: Sandfall Interactive 10 October 2026, 03:17 run.code Actor Charlie Cox, known for his role as Daredevil in Marvel projects, confirmed that he is working on an unannounced game from SEGA.

Cox did not disclose details of the project, but told an amusing story related to the start of work. According to him, when he first came to the recording, the team members unexpectedly discovered that the actor was from England, although they expected to hear an American accent.

I came to the first meeting, and everyone saw me for the first time. They offered me to voice this game, and I agreed. Then I had to record 40 hours of material or so. On the first day, I came and greeted everyone: “Hi, guys! Nice to meet you! How are you?” And then everyone reacted something like: “Oh… so he’s English.” They hoped I would be American. And now I had to record 40 hours of lines not prepared for an American accent. Charlie Cox, actor. Before this, Cox participated in the work on Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, where he played the role of Gustave — one of the central characters through whom the player gets acquainted with the events of the first chapters.

items.content:
Listen Thread 2 Link copied to clipboard Add Polygon.com on Google By Austin Manchester Published Oct 9, 2026, 10:56 AM EDT Austin Manchester is a writer and editor living in New York City. At Polygon, he covers gaming and entertainment news, reviews new video games, interviews behind-the-scenes talent, and more. He enjoys discovering hidden gems and sharing them with Polygon's audience. Previously, he was the gaming editor for AIPT Comics and has written for other outlets like XDA, How-To Geek, and The List. He enjoys soulslikes, character-driven RPGs, and third-person shooters plucked straight out of the Xbox 360 era. He also likes to flex his non-video game nerdy knowledge sometimes, whether that's explaining who's who in the new Wolverine game or recommending a comic book series about a sentient sword. News And he spent quite a bit longer recording it than he did for Clair Obscur

Image: Sandfall Interactive/Kepler Interactive Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was Daredevil: Born Again star Charlie Cox's first foray into video game voice work, and he's already finished up recording his next game. At New York Comic Con on Thursday, Cox told IGN that he'll star in an untitled upcoming game from Sega.

Cox was born in London, but his performance as the New York vigilante Matt Murdock is so convincing that the studio was surprised when he showed up for his game recording session.

"I was like, 'Hi guys, nice to meet you! How are you?' And all of them went, 'Oh, he’s English,'" Cox said. "They’d wanted [the character] to be American. But now I’ve got to do 40 hours of lines I’ve not prepared in an accent. Yeah, I think they thought I was American."

The mix-up is somewhat understandable, especially if this team at Sega hasn't played Expedition 33 yet. (They should maybe do so before the RPG leaves Xbox Game Pass .) Cox previously said his role in Expedition 33 took him around four hours to record (writer Jennifer Svedberg-Yen later said it was more like eight hours ), so based on his 40 hours spent in the booth, it sounds like he has a more central role in this Sega game.

Cox said the praise heaped on his Expedition 33 performance made him feel like a "total fraud" given how quickly he recorded his lines for Gustave. "But I'm so thrilled for the company, I'm so thrilled it did really well," he said at a convention last year . He was nominated for Best Performance at The Game Awards , but said motion-capture actor Maxence Cazorla deserved the credit. "Any nomination or any credit I get, I really have to give to him, because I believe that the performance of that character is really down to him, and my voice was just part of that process," he said.

Image: Marvel Studios Cox was at NYCC to promote Daredevil: Born Again 's third season, which will also be its last . Premiering next spring, the show will reunite Daredevil with the rest of the Defenders.

Of course, by rare I mean singular, as there's yet to be any actual game content featuring characters or world elements from Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 until now.

Announced in a Steam blog , Astral Ascent's Expedition 33: For Those Who Come After update is live now and free for all players, with the only requirement being completion of the main quest on base difficulty. Once you've got the update downloaded, you'll want to pop a seat at the new Campfire room, because you'll find some of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's best characters waiting there as special, themed summons.

Gustave is a support-type companion who heals you and gives you attack buffs, but he also has "a devastating" attack that charges up every time he's summoned. Maelle fights alongside you using a stance determined by your HP, shifting from attack to defense and unleashing a "powerful attack" that unlocks when she maintains the same stance for a while. Sciel is a card-based battler with mana regen, a basic strike attack, and a "powerful attack," each triggered under different conditions.

Meanwhile, Lune is an elemental spellcaster who syncs up with your own spell-using habits, and as is starting to become a pattern, she gets her own "powerful spell" when you summon her "enough times." Verso ranks up every time you hit an enemy and drops a rank with every hit you take, starting with an attack penalty and then building to a "massive attack bonus" as he ranks up. Finally, Monocco draws a random card from a set of five and unleashes a "powerful monster summon" based on the card he pulls.

Watch On There are also three new Expedition 33-themed rooms in Astral Ascent's crossover update: the aforementioned Campfire, the Lumière, where you square off with Petank and the Mimes with Lumière in the background, and the Gestral Village, where you face off against Golgra. Developer Hibernian Workshop says these rooms appear randomly before the final boss of each run, and you'll have the chance to pick between the Expedition 33-themed bosses or the usual Andromeda Bar, "but choose fast, it won't come back this run," warns the dev.

Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's "untranslatable" inspiration is finally getting an English release After Clair Obscur Expedition 33, Sandfall is "going to go a bit crazy" with its next game Risk of Rain inspired one of my favorite new roguelikes, and it's getting a huge update "We've wanted to do this for a long time. Getting to work with Sandfall Interactive on this crossover has been one of the best experiences we've had making Astral Ascent," the Astral Ascent team says in a statement. "Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is a game we fell in love with, like so many of you did, and this update is our way of paying tribute to it. Our biggest challenge was translating this world into our own pixel art, staying true to what makes these places feel alive while making them ours."

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 Comes To Astral Ascent In New Crossover Update
items.content:
We've been patiently hoping that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 would make its way to Switch 2 ever since it consumed our every waking hour last year. Sandfall is still yet to make that happen, but in the meantime, we have a crossover with the wonderful roguelike Astral Ascent , which we can play right now.

As revealed in today's Triple-i Initiative showcase, the sublime platforming roguelike has been treated to a bunch of crossover content from the land of Lumière. This includes three brand new bosses (Golgra, the Mime and Pétank), new rooms inspired by the game, and recruitable Expedition ally summons, each of which comes with its own special skills.

Truthfully, it looks wonderful. The crossover brings Expedition 33's world into Astral Ascent's glorious pixel art, and the trailer alone was enough to bring a tear to this writer's eye.

Here's the full rundown of everything included in the update, as detailed on the Astral Ascent Steam page:

Three Exclusive Bosses Golgra, the Mime, and Pétank have invaded the Prison, each with brand-new combat mechanics built just for this crossover. - Golgra - Calm at first, but her kicks and gestral allies get brutal once her second phase kicks in. - The Mime - Hammers, nails, walls take them both down together, or they'll revive each other. - Pétank - Runs, then rains projectiles, clones, and explosions on you.

Three New Rooms Straight from the world of Expedition 33 : Lumière , the Gestral Village , and the Campfire . One appears at random before the final boss each run: pick Expedition 33 content or the Andromeda Bar, but choose fast, it won't come back this run!

Around the Campfire Recruit a member of the Expedition as a special summon, each with their own unique mechanic: - Gustave - Heals, boosts your attack, strikes with you, and charges up a devastating finisher. - Maelle - Shifts stance with your HP; hold one long enough for a powerful payoff attack. - Sciel - Draws cards : Moon for mana, Sun for direct strikes, Twilight for a big hit. - Lune - Casts elemental spells matching your build, building to a powerful finisher. - Verso - Rank rises on hit, drops on damage taken, push it high for a massive attack bonus. - Monoco - Draws a random card, each triggering a different monster summon. You'll only get one Expedition ally per run, so take your pick, and don't forget to give Esquie a hug!

All of this is available for free to everyone who has beaten Astral Ascent on Destiny Level 0. What an excuse to dive back in, eh?

items.title: Astral Ascent x Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is live, and it adds loads of new content
items.summary: Astral Ascent just got a free Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 crossover content drop called the For those who come after Update.
items.content:
Astral Ascent just got a massive injection of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 content in a new update which just landed for free in the PC, PS, and Switch versions of the game.

There is a lot to unpack in the so-called For those who come after Update, with new stages and bosses added to the game, bringing further variety to an already content-rich action platformer.

The update includes three bosses (Golgra, the Mime, and Petank), six familiar summons to help in a pinch, and three new stages drawn directly from the world of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ( Lumière , the Gestral Village, and The Campfire).

The devs explain how the new rooms “appear at random before the world-ending boss. Each run, one world is randomly chosen where you’ll be offered the choice between the Andromeda Bar and Expedition 33 content, choose wisely, because if you pass it up, it’s gone for the rest of your run!” To access the new content, you just have to have beaten the main game. There’s also a new menu for DLC, so you can track what’s what.

Finally, Hibernian Workshop hinted at what’s next for Astral Ascent, with the promise of a new Boss Rush mode in the works. They’re not going to rush it out the door, though, so stay tuned for more updates soon!

Still with me? Of course you are! If you want to keep reading about great hand-picked roguelikes, this website is absolutely chock-full of them. Head over to the Guides Page for a concentrated hit of roguish games, organised via sub-genre and platform.

What’s more, there are always going to be new lists for emerging trends as well as fresh titles to highlight. This is because my backlog is embarrassingly long, and so I’m always trying to balance the new games that arrive in my inbox with playing the stuff I already have.

Finally, if you would like to keep track of our original reporting and support the work that we do here in this most niche corner of the Interweb, please make sure we’re one of your trusted sources on Google News . Alternatively, there’s an RSS feed , if you prefer.

You can also join our communities on Reddit and Bluesky , where I/we post all of our content and where you can share your thoughts and recommendations. We also have a burgeoning presence on YouTube . Come and say hello; we try to keep all of these spaces welcoming!

items.title: Game Pass Is About To Lose Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 And Some Other Incredible Games
items.summary: The RPG sensation and more gems are leaving in October
items.content:
Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 was one of 2025’s best games and one of the best third-party releases ever to join Game Pass day-and-date. Players have now had over a year to finish the turn-based RPG, but for any subscribers who haven’t yet taken the plunge, time is running out. The GOTY winner is leaving Game Pass on October 15.

That leaves you just under two weeks to go and complete the journey or start it from scratch. You can rush the main story to clear it in under 30 hours, but if you want to mine all of the expanded content, a completionist run will take you more than twice that. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the rare JRPG-inspired games that’s managed to break through in the modern era to a broader audience, in part thanks to its novel dodge and parry mechanics which inject some fresh energy into the usual turn-based grind. It’s also worth making it all the way through to hit the twist ending .

But Clair Obscur is also not the only great game leaving Game Pass this month . The full list includes:

Pacific Drive and A Plague Tale Requiem are both excellent, especially for the spooky month. The former is a sci-fi survival crafting game about navigating a zone full of strange anomalies with a haunted station wagon. The latter is about surviving a late medieval Europe infested with disease carrying rats. Donut County , on the other hand, is a light hearted puzzle game you can finish in just a few hours that is still one of my favorite indie games of all time.

items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text! This brings the total number of supported langua
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, is now available with Arabic text!

This brings the total number of supported languages to 20!

With the new Arabic language support, we had to consider additional changes to the game’s UI to ensure a smooth and enjoyable experience for Arabic-speaking players around the world.

Adding Arabic localization has been a true team effort over many months, from the incredible adaptation and localization work carried out by the linguists, to reworking the vast majority of the user interface for right-to-left reading, all the way through localization testing.

Every team involved brought passion and dedication to making this possible, and we couldn’t be more grateful for their work. We hope this update makes the story feel even more personal to our players.

Today’s update also includes some additional fixes and improvements. Read the full patch notes here!

Thank you all so much for your continued support! <3

Tomorrow comes.

~ The Expedition 33 Team

Following the huge demand from so many of you, we’ve been working super hard to be able to finally announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is now available in Arabic!

Content

  • New supported language (text): Arabic

    [/*]

  • Credits updated (new linguists, testers and fonts)

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Fixed an issue where applying burn after an enemy has been stunned causes them to be able to act immediately after recovering from the stun.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Cleim weapon level 10 Lumina effect that does not trigger correctly on every instance of area of effect skills.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Martenon’s Lumina effects that do not work if Sciel does not have two consecutive turns.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Sireso weapon, Level 4 Lumina, and Powerful buff, from Pictos/Luminas, applied at the start of battle may override each other depending on the character's position in combat.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Chromatic Lampmaster's AOE skill missing a sound cue on the jump attack.

    [/*]

  • Fixed Sirene's Widow Ballet missing SFX during second charm attack.

    [/*]

  • Fixed characters in combat that may have displaced heads in Photo Mode if they were not seen while turning on Photo Mode.

    [/*]

  • Various minor fixes of the UI and localizations.

    [/*]

We are aware of a crash affecting some of you when loading into the Reacher or going out of the Manor. This crash is related to some specific PC configurations. Until we fix this issue, you can work around it by setting ‘Global Illumination’ to anything below ‘Epic’ temporarily.

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team

items.title: 1st Anniversary of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33
items.summary: Expeditioners!! Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special
items.content:
Expeditioners!! 

 

Today marks 1 year since we released Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. This past year has been an incredible journey and so we have a few things to share with you today. 

 

To celebrate the occasion, the team put together a special piece of artwork that we hope you will enjoy! 

8 Million Copies Sold

We're so thrilled, and honestly still quite overwhelmed, to announce that Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 has officially reached 8 million copies sold!

Thank you so so much to every single person who has played, created art, shared, streamed, discussed, and supported this game!!

Game Update: New Haircuts + Patch Notes

We've pushed a fun little update live today: new haircuts are now available in-game, giving the expedition even more style to strut around in! 💅 

For the full list of changes, fixes, and improvements, you can read the patch notes here

Community Emotes

Our community is packed with phenomenally talented artists and we wanted to celebrate that today.  

We commissioned some of our amazing community creators to design official Expedition 33 emotes for you to use in your own channels! 

A massive thank you to IrunoArt, comickergirl (Sarah Leuver), and Bugyakis for their brilliant work on each of these!!

They're FREE to download and use here

Official Baguette Merch

In the mood to add some baguette to your wardrobe? 

We’ve partnered with Orcival and Le Béret Français to bring you the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 striped shirt and beret for your cosplays! 🥖    You can purchase the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Orcival mariniere here

And the official Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 x Le Béret Français beret is available to buy here

On top of that, keep an eye out for a limited number of units of the Monolith Set to be back in stock from our partners at Laced and Pix n' Love soon!! 

And Finally… Cake

It's been a big day for us. Thank you for making it possible. 🎂 

And if you know someone who wants to pick up the game, we're running a 20% sale right now on Steam - As well as some fun merchandise goodies available on our merch page!

Merch Page

From the bottom of our hearts, we’re so thankful to each and every one of you – this has been the best year of our lives, thanks to you. 

 

- The Expedition 33 Team

    [/*]

items.title: Patch v1.5.3 is live!
items.summary: Expeditioners! Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below: Update On Sirene Crash After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer b
items.content:
Expeditioners!

Thank you for all of your reports - the details for the fixes in this patch are written out below:

Update On Sirene Crash

  • After a thorough internal investigation, the crash that occurred after defeating Sirene can no longer be reproduced on our end. If you keep getting this issue, we’d suggest updating your Windows to the latest version. If the issue persists, please submit a report and we’ll continue investigating.

    [/*]

Bug Fixes & Improvements

Photo Mode

  • Fixed facial hair of characters being blurred in the Photo Mode on the close distance if Shading was set to Epic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue in Photo mode that prevented the Inner Cone Angle and Outer Cone Angle options from affecting the shape of the preview light source.

    [/*]

  • Photo Mode's spotlight and point light display has been modified to improve their visibility

    [/*]

Gameplay

  • Fixed an issue where loading a save while picking up a journal could cause that journal to disappear permanently and become impossible to collect again.

    • Missing journals are now also restored retroactively when loading affected saves.

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • Fixed a soft lock that could occur, during the Chromatic Glissando encounter in Sirene’s Dress level, when a dead expeditioner equipped with Shortcut and Second Chance pictos was swallowed.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on Gestral Beach where using the Rematch option after losing the volleyball minigame could create a blocked save.

    [/*]

  • Fixed a visual issue where characters affected by Inverted would not have the correct colour effect applied to their eyes.

    [/*]

Environment

  • Fixed various environment issues (collisions, misplaced assets, missing or incorrect footsteps SFX) across Verso's Drafts, the World Map, and other levels.

    [/*]

  • Fixed various lighting issues on Steam Deck in Verso’s Drafts, Endless Tower and Stone Wave Cliffs levels.

    [/*]

As always, thanks for your support and for your reports via the official Typeform - We'll continue monitoring the reports coming in and working on future fixes!

~ The Expedition 33 Team
